title: Who wrote the arrangements
summary: The band worked as a family, splitting earnings. Cottrell, Herbert Hall, Harold Holmes and Billy Douglas wrote their own, and the first arranger in 1929 was Phil Tiller; each man wrote full scores and parts.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Tim came up with something about arrangements. Did you pay the men to do arrangements?

We didn't have any money to pay ourselves nothing. Would you have a bond for everybody in the band? Well, everybody in the band worked as a family. That's what it was. If we made ten dollars, we'd split ten dollars. By the same token, if we made a hundred, we'd split a hundred. And everybody wanted the band to be the best and everybody would chip in the things that they knew how. I think Cottrell made one or two arrangements. Herbert Hall made some. And of course we had Harold Holmes, who did a tremendous job of arranging. He was one of the bass players. But the first arranger I had in the band was Phil Tiller from Little Rock, Arkansas. That was the first arranger in 1929.

There wasn't any main arrangers. Harold Holmes wrote his. Billy Douglas wrote his. And Herbert Hall. If a guy would get an idea, he would write it down. But no one was, you're referring to something like in Jimmy Luster's band, where Si Oliver was the main arranger.
Well, no, there might be five main arrangers and maybe one guy would only do two.

Well, and then you might have the thing that existed in Duke's band. Someone would write the score and Tizal would abstract it. We didn't have anything like this. The guy would write the arrangement. He would write his score and he would write each individual part for each musician.
So you didn't have any copies or anything like that? No copies. The guy would do the whole work from top to bottom. That's right. That must have had some morale in the band. Beautiful. Beautiful.

They really can. That's the thing. They got along. Beautiful as far as I can see. I never ran into a conflict where one guy would balk at doing this. Like I see today. There's no harmony there. But strange as it seems, everyone there got along real swell.
